population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. About 50.7M of ~267M US adults are on an incretin (19.0%). Age check: 0.20×9.5 + 0.33×18.3 + 0.24×29.5 + 0.23×17.5 = 1.90 + 6.04 + 7.08 + 4.03 ≈ 19.05. Income thirds 14.5/19/23.5 average 19.0. The bottom third rose most (12→14.5) because Medicaid obesity coverage expanded from 19 to 32 states. The 65+ band rose 14.5→17.5 because the Medicare Continuity Model opened to BMI ≥30 without comorbidity in Jan 2030 (≈10.7M users aged 65+). The 18–29 band barely moved: the broadcast-ad pause, the scandal and cash-only access for most young adults held it down. Payer mix of the 50.7M: diabetes- or cardiac-coded coverage ~21M (≈11M public: Medicare Part D, Medicaid, VA/TRICARE; ≈10M commercial); employer obesity coverage ~6.5M; Medicare Continuity Model obesity-only ~4.5M; Medicaid obesity ~4.0M; brand cash via TrumpRx/direct ~9.5M; gray market ~5.2M. These sum to 50.7M. Public payers cover 11 + 4.5 + 4.0 = 19.5M (38%), the largest single payer group. Commercial covers 16.5M (33%), cash 19% and gray market 10%. Off-drug population: ever 27.0% − current 19.0% = 8.0% of adults (~21M) used and are off now. Of those, ~6M stopped because of a coverage change, ~4M because of GI or other side effects (some now litigants), and the rest by choice or cost. Cycling: ~38% of current users are restarters (0.38×19.0 ≈ 7.2 pp), and ~25% of those off now had already cycled once (0.25×8.0 = 2.0 pp), so (7.2 + 2.0)/27 ≈ 34% of ever-users have stopped and restarted at least once. The rise from 31% reflects the 2028 Medicare lockout cohort returning once the lockout was cut to 6 months. Pediatric: ~0.7% of under-18s (~0.5M), flat. Medicaid 12–17 coverage grew in the expansion states, offset by under-16 obesity-only prescribing bans in nine states (about 60k adolescents moved off or never started). Roughly 1 in 4 US children lives with a parent on the drug; most children with obesity are untreated.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: from Jan 2030 the CMS Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model is national and broader. Eligibility is BMI ≥30 alone (previously BMI ≥35 or ≥30 with comorbidity). The lapse lockout is cut from 12 to 6 months. The negotiated rate steps down from $245 to $215/month, and the beneficiary copay stays $50. The adherence conditions remain: ≥80% proportion of days covered, and ≥5% loss at 6 months. Obesity-only enrolment is ~4.5M by Dec 2030. Run-rate spending is 4.5M × $215 × 12 ≈ $11.6B/yr. Calendar-2030 outlay is ≈ 3.2M average enrolees × $215 × 12 ≈ $8.3B, about double the ~$4B/yr CBO baseline for the original pilot, which is now a live budget fight. Medicaid: 32 states cover obesity at the $215 multistate rate for ~4.0M enrolees. Gross cost is 4.0M × $215 × 12 ≈ $10.3B/yr; the federal share at ~65% blended FMAP is ≈ $6.7B. Eleven of the 32 states attach Continuity-style adherence conditions. Public payers (Medicare, Medicaid, VA/TRICARE, all indications) now pay for ~38% of users, the largest single payer group.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ generic semaglutide brands at ~$7–35/month, and generic oral semaglutide has been on sale there since late 2028. China has had domestic semaglutide generics since 2026 and is now exporting API. Canada, Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generics at roughly CAD 60–100 or local equivalents. Tirzepatide and amycretin are not generic anywhere major. US exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: The managed decline continued. TrumpRx and direct cash prices: Wegovy pill and Foundayo starting doses $149; injectable semaglutide $179–199; Zepbound $249; oral amycretin (launched May 2030) $249; retatrutide cut from $399 to $299 in a Jun 2029 TrumpRx renegotiation. List prices are unchanged (Wegovy $1,349) and almost nobody pays them. Employer weight-management coverage fell 44%→38% (Business Group on Health, 2030). Employers cite the Medicare and Medicaid expansion and $149–249 oral cash prices as reasons to exclude obesity-only use; most remaining coverage is code-restricted. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers still run BMI surcharges. The gray market shrank slightly (6M→5.2M users, ~10%) as sub-$200 brand orals and public coverage absorbed price-sensitive users. Research-peptide retatrutide, and since 2030 'research' amycretin, kept the gym and recomposition segment. New starts are ~55% oral (35% in 2028), but most continuing users are still on weekly pens, so the stock is mixed.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (amycretin oral, Novo; approved Apr 2030)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (semaglutide, Sep 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: nicotine cessation in normal-weight smokers and vapers
alcohol reduction: phase 3 AUD trial positive (Dec 2029), sNDA filed Apr 2030, FDA decision expected 2031; widely prescribed off-label meanwhile
microdosing for 'metabolic health' via gray-market telehealth
research-peptide retatrutide and amycretin in gym and recomposition communities
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care (now illegal for obesity-only use in nine states, along with ages 12–15)
drugs.pipeline_note: Oral parity was realised within the approval rules. Novo filed oral and subcutaneous amycretin in Feb 2029. The FDA approved oral amycretin in Apr 2030, after a standard review extended by a pharmacovigilance inspection that followed the Novo documents scandal. It averages ~21% loss at 68 weeks, statistically indistinguishable from tirzepatide in an indirect comparison, and is the first pill to match a leading injectable. It does not match retatrutide (~29%), which remains the efficacy ceiling. Its label lists emotional blunting/anhedonia (≈3% vs ≈1% placebo) among adverse reactions. Subcutaneous amycretin is under review, with a decision in 2031. Survodutide was filed Jul 2029 and is under review, with a decision in early 2031; it is not on the market. MariTide (monthly) is in phase 3 with filing expected 2031; it is not on the market. The semaglutide AUD sNDA was filed Apr 2030 and is undecided; no new indication was approved in the window. The global incretin market is ~$135B (2030), with volume up and unit price down. Lilly leads US share. Novo's US position rests on the Wegovy pill and oral amycretin and is clouded by litigation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Oral amycretin's nausea rates are similar to tirzepatide's. Many of the ~4M side-effect stoppers are now solicited by plaintiff firms.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. FDA Sep 2029 guidance requires consumer materials to name gastroparesis and ileus explicitly.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis / persistent delayed gastric emptying and ileus (including reports persisting after discontinuation)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Ileus is labelled (2023). Persistent gastroparesis after stopping is contested: case series exist, but no controlled confirmation. The MDL in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania passed ~41,000 filed and tolled claims by Dec 2030, up from ~3,000 in 2025, which makes it a mass tort. The first bellwether (Oct 2029, pre-2023-label plaintiff) returned a $38M verdict against Novo on failure to warn; it is under appeal. Two further bellwethers are set for 2031.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letter to Novo (Jul 2029) on postmarketing adverse-event reporting practices. A label update strengthening gastroparesis language is pending. No settlement fund as of Dec 2030.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still no causal confirmation in long RCTs, and absolute risk is low. About 9,000 pancreatitis claims ride alongside the gastroparesis docket. Pancreatic-cancer claims were filed in 2030 but have weak epidemiological support.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Folded into the litigation. No regulatory change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss, and highest in retatrutide real-world use.
More older adults on drugs after the Medicare expansion keep it in focus. Lower bone density in women over 60 on long-term use remains associational (suspected) in 2029–30 cohorts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide and amycretin labels recommend resistance exercise and protein counselling. The Continuity Model added an optional DXA benefit in 2030. No class warning.
EMA 'very rare' label; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: AUD trial psychiatric monitoring found no excess.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Quantified for the first time. The semaglutide AUD phase 3 (Dec 2029) included the Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale as a safety endpoint. Clinically meaningful new anhedonia appeared in ~3.5% on drug vs ~1.2% on placebo; it was mostly dose-related and largely resolved within 8–12 weeks of dose reduction. The oral amycretin programme found ~3% vs ~1%. Treated as uncommon.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed under Adverse Reactions, not Warnings, on the oral amycretin label (Apr 2030) and in a semaglutide label update (Aug 2030). Obesity Medicine Association guidance (2030) recommends a brief anhedonia screen at titration visits.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Roughly half of lost weight returns within a year. Shortening the Medicare lockout to 6 months reduced, but did not end, forced cycling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; still the rationale for adherence conditions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Reports continue at retatrutide-level intake reduction.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The interim FDA Sentinel cycling analysis (2030) found no cardiovascular excess from cycling beyond regain itself, but body-composition substudies suggest regain is fat-weighted. Adolescent users who started in 2023–24 begin crossing five years in 2028–29, and data are thin.
FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~6,500 by late 2030. 'Research' amycretin appeared within weeks of approval.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts continue; personal importation still mostly unpoliced; FTC actions against six telehealth advertisers (2030).

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous GLP-1 RA use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A UK CPRD replication (2029) found a hazard ratio of ~1.3, weaker than the Nordic ~1.5. Absolute excess is ~2 per 1,000 person-years after year 5. Confounding by diabetes duration has still not been excluded.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded Mar 2029: hyposmia added to EU semaglutide SmPC as an uncommon adverse reaction. FDA has made no US label change; Sentinel review is ongoing.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~30% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down ~5–6% from 2026 and sugary drinks ~4–5%. Protein, fibre and small-format SKUs keep growing. Companion lines are now a standard CPG category. Medicare expansion moved the shift into older, rural households, hitting regional bakery and canned-dessert brands, and two Midwest private-label snack plants closed in 2029.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down a further ~3% over the window. The positive AUD trial and widespread off-label prescribing name heavy drinkers as the lost segment. Beer is down slightly. Non-alc keeps growing. Cigarette volume declines accelerated by about a point a year above trend, and Altria's investor materials quantify incretin cessation for the first time.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and tickets are supported by premium small plates. Half-portion menus are standard. Buffet chains keep closing locations. Senior-heavy casual-dining formats (cafeterias, family-style chains) in the South and Midwest saw the sharpest ticket declines after the Medicare expansion.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Body-liberation marketing gets cultural attention but no volume. Re-buying in smaller sizes is now driven by older shoppers.

fitness.state: Strength and 'muscle-preservation' programmes keep growing, including Medicare Advantage-sponsored senior strength classes. Big-box cardio gyms are flat. Research-peptide sales still run through gym communities.

insurance.state: Employer obesity coverage is down to 38%, with commercial coverage concentrated on diabetic and cardiac codes. Public payers now cover the largest share of users. Medicare Advantage plans market Continuity enrolment support and strength benefits. BMI surcharges persist at about 1 in 5 large self-funded employers. Commercial pharmacy trend is ~7%.

pharma.state: Lilly is dominant. Novo regained some US volume with the Wegovy pill and oral amycretin, but took a ~25% share-price drawdown after the Jun 2029 documents, faces a $38M bellwether verdict and ~41,000 claims, and has booked a litigation provision. Total revenue keeps growing on volume while per-unit prices fall. Plaintiff-firm TV ad spend on GLP-1 injury now exceeds manufacturers' suspended broadcast spend.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among older Americans, especially in the South and Midwest, a smaller body now reads as 'on the Medicare one'. In affluent suburbs, thinness after 40 is assumed to be pharmacological. A larger body is read three ways: refusal, a coverage gap, or, newly, someone who 'got hurt by it' and stopped.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Public expansion narrowed the income gap without closing it (on-drug rates 23.5% top third vs 14.5% bottom). The poor are increasingly covered by public plans with adherence conditions, the middle by $149–249 cash pills, and the top by commercial plans or by retatrutide at $299. Surveillance falls on the publicly covered and on hourly workers with BMI surcharges.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Half portions are normal well beyond the coasts. Church suppers in East Tennessee and Oklahoma have split into on-drug and off-drug tables, often by generation now that grandparents are on Medicare's drug. The 'Made Whole' movement holds 'full table' Sunday dinners in Tulsa and Fort Worth as open acts of witness.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On it / off it' is a standard app filter in large metros. The 2030 label language on emotional blunting gave couples a sentence to point to, and therapists now ask about dose. Libido is still mostly not attributed to the drug.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of all kinds remains officially treatable, but the scandal and the lawsuits gave the counter-movement evidence instead of only sentiment. Atlanta fat-liberation organisers, Tulsa 'Made Whole' congregations and MAHA-aligned 'natural body' influencers all cite the Novo documents and the anhedonia label. They draw opposite conclusions: civil rights, sin and pharma fraud. 'Bodies Aren't Billing Codes' marched on HHS in Washington in Apr 2030.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: It is now measured and labelled as uncommon. The semaglutide AUD trial found ~3.5% vs ~1.2% new clinically meaningful anhedonia on the SHAPS, and oral amycretin ~3% vs ~1%; both were mostly dose-related and reversible with dose reduction. Milder sub-threshold flattening, the 'calmer' many users describe, is still unmeasured and sits below the label's definition.
interior_life.framing: A side effect: uncommon, dose-related and manageable. Clinics now ask about it, and the answer either leads to dose reduction or is filed as the expected reduction in craving. Most users still call any quieting maturity.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Some employee-assistance programmes added 'medication-related low mood' to their intake menus. Sales managers' complaints about flat closers now occasionally reference the label, but no employer policy addresses it. Wellness vendors still praise fewer smoke breaks.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: A small genre of essays and songs about 'coming back' after a dose cut appeared in 2030. Middle-aged league bowling and bar trivia membership keeps thinning. High-intensity live formats remain in vogue. A Nashville songwriter's album about tapering down was a minor hit.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists screen for dose and agent. The anhedonia label gave patients a reason to ask prescribers for step-downs. Desire specifically is not on any label.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The label cut both ways. Body-liberation and MAHA groups say 'they admitted it'. Mainstream clinicians say '3 percent, reversible', which contains the issue. Participation shows no measurable effect, and the rhetoric of 'sedating the workforce' persists on the right-populist fringe.

state.regulatory_posture: Expansionary on payment and restrictive at the edges. CMS widened public coverage and cut the price. The FDA approved oral amycretin, issued Novo a pharmacovigilance warning letter and tightened GI disclosure. HHS brokered a suspension of manufacturer broadcast and influencer advertising for weight-management drugs (Sep 2029). Nine states, led by Tennessee and Oklahoma, enacted under-16 obesity-only prescribing bans. Personal importation is still largely unpoliced.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. The Medicare Continuity Model is national at $215/$50 with BMI ≥30 eligibility. Thirty-two Medicaid programmes cover obesity. Public payers are now the default for older and poorer users, with continued coverage contingent on demonstrated adherence and response.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Continuity Model and 11 Medicaid programmes require ≥80% refill adherence and ≥5% loss at 6 months, now with a 6-month lockout on lapse instead of 12. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers run BMI surcharges ($50–100/month) waived on connected-pen or refill verification; vendors increasingly accept pharmacy receipts for cash orals. Texas's ban on BMI surcharges in state-regulated plans still exempts ERISA plans. Colorado and Illinois bills to bar employer access to connected-pen data stalled in 2030.
state.workforce_or_military: Army and Air Force accession waivers for GLP-1-assisted recruits continue with ≥6 months of off-drug weight stability. TRICARE covers obesity use for active duty only. The VA expanded obesity coverage for veterans enrolled in its MOVE! programme in 2029.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US price gap with India (~$149–199 vs ~$7–35) still drives the gray market, now joined by Chinese semaglutide API. The Novo scandal became a Danish political issue, with parliamentary questions over the state-linked Novo Nordisk Foundation's stewardship. Lilly and Novo still trade US price concessions for tariff relief; the retatrutide cut to $299 was part of a 2029 round.

events.event: Tennessee and Oklahoma become the first of nine states to ban prescribing GLP-1 drugs for obesity alone to anyone under 16, after a session in which 'Made Whole' pastors and MAHA-aligned parents testified; pediatric endocrinologists warn that about 60,000 teenagers will lose access.

Documents unsealed in the federal GLP-1 multidistrict litigation in Philadelphia show Novo Nordisk safety staff in 2018–21 coding hundreds of spontaneous gastroparesis reports under milder terms and shelving a proposed gastric-emptying study; the FDA issues a warning letter on Novo's postmarketing reporting in July, and in September Novo and Lilly agree with HHS to suspend US TV and influencer ads for weight-management drugs.

A Philadelphia federal jury awards $38 million to a former Ozempic user in the first gastroparesis bellwether; Novo appeals, and filed and tolled claims in the docket climb past 41,000 by the end of 2030, including about 9,000 alleging pancreatitis.

Novo's phase 3 alcohol-use-disorder trial of semaglutide meets its drinking endpoints and, in the first incretin trial to measure it, records new clinically meaningful anhedonia in 3.5% of participants vs 1.2% on placebo, largely reversed by lowering the dose; the FDA adds emotional blunting to semaglutide's adverse-reactions section in August 2030.

CMS takes its Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model national, opening it to any beneficiary with a BMI of 30 or more, cutting the lapse lockout to six months and lowering the negotiated rate from $245 to $215; with 32 state Medicaid programmes now covering obesity, public payers become the largest source of GLP-1 coverage in the US.

The FDA approves Novo's oral amycretin, a daily pill that averaged about 21% weight loss in trials, on par with weekly tirzepatide injections; it launches in May at $249 a month on TrumpRx, with emotional blunting listed among its adverse reactions.

open_tensions: Public payers are now the default for older and poorer users, at a run-rate (~$11.6B Medicare + ~$10.3B Medicaid gross) far above the original CBO baseline. Coverage is still conditioned on refill and weigh-in surveillance. The 2031 budget fight and the 2031–32 generic window will decide whether the public programme is rationed harder or repriced.

Over 41,000 gastroparesis and pancreatitis claims, a Novo verdict under appeal and an unsettled document scandal sit beside a pill from the same company that the public programme increasingly pays for. Whether Novo settles, and whether the FDA strengthens class GI labelling, is open.

Emotional blunting is now an acknowledged, uncommon side effect, just as the FDA weighs a 2031 alcohol indication that sells the same mechanism as therapy. The agency will have to say where reduced craving ends and anhedonia begins.

Nine states bar obesity-only prescribing to under-16s while Medicaid covers 12–17-year-olds elsewhere. The first adolescent cohort is crossing five years of use as the hyposmia signal stays unresolved in the US and labelled in Europe.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, with oral initial doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) at $149/month.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.
Texas's 2027 ban on BMI-based premium surcharges still applies only to state-regulated plans, leaving ERISA self-funded employers free to charge them.

prose.headline: Medicare Is Now America's Weight-Loss Insurer. The Pill Is Here. So Are the Lawyers, and Your Refill Clock.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 about 51 million American adults, roughly one in five, take an incretin drug. The more important change is who pays. For the first time the largest payer is not an employer but the government. In January CMS opened its Medicare Continuity Model to any beneficiary with a BMI of 30, cut the price it pays from $245 to $215 a month and kept the $50 copay. Thirty-two state Medicaid programmes now cover obesity. Public money pays for nearly four in ten users. Employers keep retreating. Just 38 percent still cover weight management at all, and most of them only under a diabetes or heart code. They point to Medicare and to $149 pills as reasons not to bother.

The public coverage still comes with conditions. A beneficiary who misses too many refills, or fails to lose five percent in six months, loses coverage for six months, down from twelve. Medicare does not pay for weight-loss drugs outright; it pays for proven adherence and response. The result is that grandparents in Knoxville and Tulsa now have pharmacy apps with green rings, and they check them.

The needle barrier is mostly gone. In April the FDA approved Novo Nordisk's oral amycretin, a daily pill that takes off about as much weight as a weekly tirzepatide injection. More than half of new patients now start on a pill. Lilly's retatrutide, still the strongest drug at nearly 30 percent loss, came down to $299 in a tariff-linked price round. Brand prices keep stepping down through negotiated channels and never fall far enough to make coverage irrelevant. Indian generics at a tenth of the price still reach about five million Americans by mail.

Novo sells that pill under a cloud. In June 2029, documents unsealed in the federal litigation in Philadelphia showed its safety staff, years earlier, filing gastroparesis reports under gentler codes and shelving a study that might have measured the problem. The FDA sent a warning letter. A jury awarded one plaintiff $38 million. Claims have passed 41,000. The drug ads disappeared from television after an HHS-brokered pause, and the injury-lawyer ads took over the same slots. Nobody has shown that the drugs permanently paralyse stomachs, but that question will now be settled in court as well as in journals.

The counter-movement found its evidence. Fat-liberation organisers in Atlanta, 'Made Whole' congregations in Tulsa and MAHA-aligned influencers marched separately on HHS in April. All three cite the Novo documents and reach incompatible conclusions. Their most concrete win came in the states. Tennessee, Oklahoma and seven others banned prescribing for obesity alone to anyone under sixteen. In those states a fifteen-year-old cannot get the drug his grandmother's Medicare pays for.

The quiet complaint of 2026 got a number. Novo's alcohol trial, the first to measure pleasure, found new clinically meaningful anhedonia in 3.5 percent of patients against about 1 percent on placebo, mostly reversed by lowering the dose. It is now on two labels under adverse reactions, not warnings. Clinics ask about it at titration. That move from unmentioned to uncommon pleases nobody. Critics say the companies admitted it. Clinicians say it affects three percent and goes away with a dose cut. Users mostly go on calling it maturity.

Snack and spirits volumes keep slipping, buffets keep closing, and cafeteria chains in the South have lost their senior lunch crowd. Cigarette sales are falling faster than trend. Nothing has collapsed. The country is a little lighter, a little more sober, more watched by its own pharmacy and more often paid for by Washington.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Darlene Pruitt sets the pill on the windowsill at 6:10 and swallows it with four ounces of tap water, measured in the cup she keeps for it. Then she waits the half hour before coffee and watches the light come up over the Kroger lot. The pharmacy app shows a green ring at 94 percent. She checks it the way her mother checked the thermostat.

At nine she drives to the clinic on Kingston Pike for the six-month weigh-in. The nurse doesn't say the number until she has typed it in. Six point one. 'You're good, Miss Darlene.' Darlene hadn't known she was holding her breath.

On the waiting-room television a man in a navy suit asks whether you or a loved one were diagnosed with stomach paralysis after taking Ozempic or Wegovy. The drug commercials went away last fall. The lawyer ads stayed.

Lunch is half a pimento cheese sandwich. She wraps the other half for Tyler, who will eat it standing at the counter after school and then make another. He is fifteen and six-foot-one. His pediatrician said the word 'law' twice and 'next birthday' once.

Kayla calls on her break from the distribution center. The surcharge is on her pay stub again, seventy-five dollars, because the pen app didn't sync. She's switching to the pill, the $149 one, so she can just upload the receipt.

At Wednesday supper at First Baptist the banana pudding comes round and Darlene passes it on. Ruthie Cole, who isn't on anything, takes two spoonfuls and looks at her as if she has said something out loud.

That night Darlene falls asleep easily. She has stopped thinking of that as news.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid obesity coverage expanded from 19 to 32 states
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: 13 states add a costly obesity benefit in two years, with no budget, federal-match or political cause shown beyond the stipulated driver, and it roughly triples enrollees from 1.5M to 4.0M.

least_plausible_claims.quote: the FDA adds emotional blunting to semaglutide's adverse-reactions section in August 2030.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the label change comes only eight months after the trial readout and four months after the sNDA filing, with no safety-labeling pathway shown. The FDA has already labelled hyposmia only slowly.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Indian generics at a tenth of the price still reach about five million Americans by mail.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world state says the ~5.2M gray-market users are split across Indian/Turkish imports, 503A compounding and research peptides. The prose attributes all of them to Indian generics, so it contradicts the world state.

rationale.badness: This is a harder but not collapsing world. Public expansion narrows the income gap (bottom third 12→14.5), and anhedonia is now measured and labelled, which lowers the epistemic score. Real costs remain: refill and weigh-in surveillance of the publicly covered, connected-pen BMI surcharges ($75 on Kayla's stub), nine under-16 prescribing bans, a 41,000-claim GI litigation docket, and church tables split by generation.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visibly realised. Public expansion is the Medicare/Medicaid growth, the litigation and Novo documents scandal are in the events, oral parity is amycretin approved 14 months after filing, and restriction is the nine-state bans plus adherence conditions. The restriction is partly offset by the shortened lockout, and no new indication is approved, as required. mechanism: Most changes have chains, but the Medicaid jump from 19 to 32 states (claim 1) and the very fast Aug 2030 label change (claim 2) are asserted rather than shown, and the prose overstates Indian generics (claim 3). magnitude: Every figure sits inside the envelope (19.0% on drug, 27.0% ever used). The payer mix sums to 50.7M, the Medicare ($11.6B) and Medicaid ($10.3B gross, $6.7B federal) arithmetic holds, and the cycling arithmetic is correct at 34%. Only minor looseness remains, such as the Medicare enrolment tripling in one year.
rationale.generativity: The Darlene vignette is dense with usable detail: the green-ring app, 4 oz of water, the six-month weigh-in, the lawyer ads, Tyler's pediatrician saying 'law' twice, Kayla's pen-sync surcharge and the banana pudding at First Baptist. The world fields support many scenes across Medicare, church, workplace and clinic, though the closing beat is a little tidy.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Indian generics at a tenth of the price still reach about five million Americans by mail.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: The world note says the 5.2M gray-market users are split across personal importation, 503A compounding and research peptides. Prose credits Indian generics alone with about 5M, which contradicts that split. The 'tenth of the price' figure also does not match the $60–120 import price in the parent world.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third rose most (12→14.5) because Medicaid obesity coverage expanded from 19 to 32 states.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: 13 states adding obesity coverage in two years is asserted, with no state budget, waiver or political path shown. The Medicaid population goes from 1.5M to 4.0M at the same time as the rate is cut from $245 to $215. Only the Medicare expansion has a visible causal chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The first bellwether (Oct 2029, pre-2023-label plaintiff) returned a $38M verdict against Novo on failure to warn
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: A federal MDL bellwether verdict about four months after the June 2029 document unsealing is very fast. Discovery, Daubert rulings and trial normally take longer. The claim count growing from ~3,000 to ~41,000 is aggressive but is covered by the litigation driver.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder but not collapsing society. Access widens through Medicare and Medicaid, but coverage stays conditioned on refill and weigh-in surveillance (state/conditioning, Kayla's $75 surcharge when the pen app fails). Under-16 bans, litigation over gastroparesis and eating-ritual splits (church tables) add cohesion and autonomy costs. Epistemic harm eases because anhedonia is now measured and labelled. Inequality narrows only partly (23.5% top vs 14.5% bottom).
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible. Public expansion comes through the Medicare and Medicaid changes, the litigation and scandal chain is traceable through events, and oral parity is realised through the amycretin filing and approval inside the allowed window. The state_action restriction is carried mainly by the nine under-16 bans, while the lockout cut and Medicaid expansion pull the other way, so that driver is only partly clean. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including scandal to ads pause to label to counter-movement, and Medicare eligibility to the 65+ rise. Claims 1 and 2 are asserted or inconsistent, and the Medicaid expansion and the quick bellwether (claim 3) have thin causes. The 2028 lockout cohort 'returning once the lockout was cut' in 2030 is also muddled. magnitude: Adoption (19.0), ever-used (27.0), income thirds and age bands all sit inside the envelope and reconcile. The payer mix sums to 50.7M, the Medicare ($11.6B run-rate, $8.3B calendar) and Medicaid ($10.3B gross, $6.7B federal) figures multiply out, and the cycling arithmetic gives 34%. The amycretin timing (filed Feb 2029, approved Apr 2030) respects the 12-month rule. No generic is introduced in the US.
rationale.generativity: The day-in-the-life gives concrete, specific scenes: Darlene's 4 oz of water and the pharmacy app's green ring, the six-month weigh-in, the lawyer ads, Tyler's age against the ban, Kayla's surcharge and the pen-app sync, and the banana pudding at church. They tie back to world fields such as the Medicare conditioning, the bans, the surcharges and the split supper tables. Several implied characters could carry scenes, and the texture is strong.

least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: enrolment triples from 1.5M in one year. The prior rule already admitted BMI ≥30 with comorbidity, which covers most older adults with obesity, so dropping the comorbidity requirement should add far fewer than 3M, and no uptake mechanism is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Subcutaneous amycretin is under review, with a decision in 2031.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the note says oral and subcutaneous amycretin were filed together in Feb 2029. The oral form was approved after about 14 months, yet the injectable is left under review for roughly 2.5 years with no stated reason.

least_plausible_claims.quote: 32 states cover obesity at the $215 multistate rate for ~4.0M enrolees.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: 13 more state Medicaid programmes add obesity-drug coverage in two years, a multi-billion-dollar commitment, and the candidate shows no budget or political chain for it beyond the federal price and the stipulated coverage driver.

rationale.badness: The world is harder than 2028 but not much worse. Autonomy is squeezed by adherence surveillance (refill rings, pen-sync surcharges such as Kayla's $75) and by under-16 bans in nine states that cut off about 60k teenagers. Cohesion suffers from split church suppers, a polarised backlash and a mass tort. Inequality narrows with public coverage (bottom third 14.5% vs top 23.5%) and reward blunting is now measured and labelled, which lowers the epistemic score, but conditioned benefits, regain from cycling and cash-tier gaps remain.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable. Public expansion shows in Medicare and Medicaid, litigation in the MDL and the $38M verdict, oral parity in oral amycretin, the scandal in the June 2029 documents, the backlash in the marches, restriction in the under-16 bans, and the niche side effect in the 3.5% vs 1.2% anhedonia figure. No new indication is approved, which respects the empty new_indications driver. mechanism: most changes have chains, but the Medicare tripling to 4.5M, the 13-state Medicaid expansion and the slow subcutaneous amycretin review are asserted rather than shown (claims 1–3). The cycling rise attributed to a lockout cohort returning 'once the lockout was cut' is also loose, since the cut came in Jan 2030. magnitude: adults on drug 19.0% and ever used 27.0% are inside the envelope, the age, income and payer figures sum correctly, and the Medicare ($11.6B run-rate, $8.3B calendar) and Medicaid ($10.3B gross, $6.7B federal) arithmetic checks. Amycretin approval is 14 months after filing, within the rules, and no US generic appears.
rationale.generativity: The prose supplies Darlene's measured water and green-ring app, the nurse's weigh-in, Kayla's pen-sync surcharge, Tyler caught by the under-16 ban, and the banana pudding at First Baptist. least_plausible_claims.quote: the FDA adds emotional blunting to semaglutide's adverse-reactions section in August 2030.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the label change comes only eight months after the trial readout and four months after the sNDA filing, with no safety-labeling pathway shown. The FDA has already labelled hyposmia only slowly.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Indian generics at a tenth of the price still reach about five million Americans by mail.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world state says the ~5.2M gray-market users are split across Indian/Turkish imports, 503A compounding and research peptides. The prose attributes all of them to Indian generics, so it contradicts the world state.

rationale.badness: This is a harder but not collapsing world. Public expansion narrows the income gap (bottom third 12→14.5), and anhedonia is now measured and labelled, which lowers the epistemic score. Real costs remain: refill and weigh-in surveillance of the publicly covered, connected-pen BMI surcharges ($75 on Kayla's stub), nine under-16 prescribing bans, a 41,000-claim GI litigation docket, and church tables split by generation.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visibly realised. Public expansion is the Medicare/Medicaid growth, the litigation and Novo documents scandal are in the events, oral parity is amycretin approved 14 months after filing, and restriction is the nine-state bans plus adherence conditions. The restriction is partly offset by the shortened lockout, and no new indication is approved, as required. mechanism: Most changes have chains, but the Medicaid jump from 19 to 32 states (claim 1) and the very fast Aug 2030 label change (claim 2) are asserted rather than shown, and the prose overstates Indian generics (claim 3). magnitude: Every figure sits inside the envelope (19.0% on drug, 27.0% ever used). The payer mix sums to 50.7M, the Medicare ($11.6B) and Medicaid ($10.3B gross, $6.7B federal) arithmetic holds, and the cycling arithmetic is correct at 34%. Only minor looseness remains, such as the Medicare enrolment tripling in one year.
rationale.generativity: The Darlene vignette is dense with usable detail: the green-ring app, 4 oz of water, the six-month weigh-in, the lawyer ads, Tyler's pediatrician saying 'law' twice, Kayla's pen-sync surcharge and the banana pudding at First Baptist. The world fields support many scenes across Medicare, church, workplace and clinic, though the closing beat is a little tidy.
